summary: Electronic Arts' long-running racing franchise, from exotic-road racing through street racing, sim-leaning Shift entries, online/mobile spin-offs, and remasters.

entries.title: The Need for Speed
entries.definitive_edition: The Need for Speed: Special Edition

emulation.emulator: Retro PC/VM or DOSBox for DOS comparison
emulation.notes: Use Windows compatibility tooling for the primary and DOSBox/3DO emulation only for comparison.

primary.version: The Need for Speed: Special Edition
primary.why: The 1996 PC Special Edition adds PC-era extras and gives the original game the best capture/upscaling route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows Special Edition on a configured retro PC/VM route; use the 3DO release only for first-release history.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster; preserve the PC Special Edition separately from the 3DO original.

entries.title: Nissan Presents: Over Drivin' GT-R

emulation.notes: Use Saturn emulation for capture if original hardware is unavailable.

primary.why: This is a Japan-only Nissan-focused localized retail variant of the first Need for Speed, so original Saturn hardware or Saturn emulation is the only route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Japanese Saturn release via original hardware or Mednafen/SSF-style Saturn emulation.

entries.remaster_caveats: Preservation entry; no remaster.

entries.title: Nissan Presents: Over Drivin' Skyline Memorial

emulation.notes: Use high internal resolution for the PlayStation-only release.

primary.why: This Japan-only Nissan Skyline-focused variant is documented as a PlayStation release only.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Japanese PlayStation release on original hardware or DuckStation with high internal resolution.

entries.remaster_caveats: Preservation entry; no remaster.

entries.title: Need for Speed II
entries.definitive_edition: Need for Speed II: Special Edition

emulation.notes: Use PC route for main play, PlayStation emulation only for comparison.

primary.version: Need for Speed II: Special Edition
primary.why: The PC Special Edition is the most complete and highest-fidelity route for the second game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows Special Edition with modern compatibility fixes; use PlayStation only for console comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster.

entries.title: Need for Speed: V-Rally

emulation.notes: Use platform emulators only for console/handheld comparison.

primary.why: The Windows release gives the best fidelity for EA's North American Need for Speed-branded version of the first V-Rally.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version for main preservation; use PlayStation for the original EA-branded North American release context.

entries.remaster_caveats: Part of the standalone V-Rally lineage; include here because EA marketed it under Need for Speed in North America.

entries.title: Need for Speed III: Hot Pursuit

primary.why: The Windows version is the highest-fidelity route and preserves the classic Hot Pursuit formula.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with compatibility fixes; use DuckStation only for PlayStation comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster of this specific 1998 game.

entries.title: Need for Speed: High Stakes

primary.why: The Windows version is the highest-fidelity route and preserves the expanded career and damage-model era.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with compatibility fixes and widescreen/community patches where documented.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster.

entries.title: Need for Speed: V-Rally 2

primary.why: The Windows version is the highest-fidelity route for EA's Need for Speed-branded North American release of V-Rally 2.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release; use PlayStation/Dreamcast only for console comparison and regional branding history.

entries.remaster_caveats: Standalone V-Rally lineage; included due to Need for Speed branding in North America.

entries.title: Need for Speed: Porsche Unleashed
entries.definitive_edition: Windows release plus PlayStation secondary sample

emulation.emulator: Windows compatibility tooling; DuckStation for secondary
emulation.notes: Use Windows for main play and DuckStation for PlayStation-only content.

primary.why: The Windows version has the strongest fidelity and the Porsche-focused career/factory-driver structure, while the PlayStation version is different enough to preserve separately.
primary.how_to_play: Play Windows as the main route with compatibility fixes; play PlayStation only for its exclusive/different chase-mode and structure.

secondary.exclusive_content: Different Eden Studios console rendition with exclusive chase-mode/structure differences.
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the PlayStation-exclusive chase-mode and console-specific progression.
secondary.why: The PlayStation version is a distinct rendition rather than a straight PC down-port.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster; document Porsche licensing and version differences.

entries.title: Motor City Online

emulation.notes: Server-dependent Windows game; no official live service.

primary.why: This was a Windows-only online racing MMO originally conceived as Need for Speed: Motor City, so it is archived as a preservation/shutdown entry.
primary.how_to_play: No official live route remains; document original client/server history and any legal archival route separately.

entries.remaster_caveats: Servers went offline; treat as preservation history.

entries.title: Need for Speed: Web Racing

emulation.notes: Requires preserved web/service environment if recoverable.

primary.why: This online-only conversion reused Need for Speed III content through EA.com's Platinum service, so it is a preservation-only web entry.
primary.how_to_play: No normal current play route; archive only if a verified web build and service wrapper are preserved.

entries.remaster_caveats: Online-only service entry; no remaster.

entries.title: Need for Speed: Top Speed

emulation.notes: Requires preserved web/service environment if recoverable.

primary.why: This was an online-only promotional game tied to AOL Games/Pogo and the IMAX film Top Speed, so original web preservation is the only route.
primary.how_to_play: No normal current play route; archive only if a verified playable web build exists.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster; promotional online game.

entries.title: Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit 2

emulation.notes: Use high internal resolution and widescreen only if verified stable.

primary.why: The PlayStation 2 version is a distinctly different Black Box rendition and the lead-console version; PCSX2 upscaling gives it the best fidelity/completeness balance.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation 2 version in PCSX2 with high internal resolution; sample the EA Seattle PC/GameCube/Xbox version only if comparing the alternate build.

secondary.exclusive_content: Distinct EA Seattle version with different progression and content structure.
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the alternate EA Seattle version if documenting differences.
secondary.why: The game has separate PS2 and non-PS2 renditions.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not confuse with the 2010 Hot Pursuit reboot or its remaster.

entries.title: Need for Speed: Underground

emulation.notes: Native Windows route; PCSX2/Dolphin/xemu optional for comparison.

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity and most configurable route for the first Underground era entry.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with compatibility/widescreen fixes; use console versions only for comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster.

entries.title: Need for Speed: Underground 2

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route for the open-city Underground sequel and supports modern compatibility fixes.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with widescreen/compatibility fixes; preserve handheld/mobile versions as adaptations only.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster.

entries.title: Need for Speed: Underground Rivals

emulation.notes: Use high internal resolution for capture.

primary.why: This PSP spin-off has PSP-specific tracks and design, so PPSSPP upscaling is the best route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PSP release in PPSSPP at high internal resolution.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster.

entries.title: Need for Speed: Most Wanted

primary.why: The Black Edition adds bonus cars/challenges on the PC route, making it the best fidelity/completeness pick for the 2005 game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows Black Edition with compatibility/widescreen fixes; treat PSP 5-1-0 as a separate spin-off.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not conflate with the 2012 Criterion reboot using the same subtitle.

entries.title: Need for Speed: Most Wanted 5-1-0

primary.why: The PSP spin-off has a separate feature mix including Tuner Takedown and lacks some console/PC elements, so it is preserved as its own game.
primary.how_to_play: Play in PPSSPP at high internal resolution after the Windows Black Edition main game.

entries.remaster_caveats: Separate from the 2005 console/PC Most Wanted.

entries.title: Need for Speed: Carbon

primary.why: Windows provides the highest-fidelity route for the main Carbon campaign; the portable Own the City release is different enough to archive separately.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with compatibility fixes; then play Carbon - Own the City separately for its different story/setting.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster; keep the portable companion separate.

entries.title: Need for Speed: Carbon - Own the City

primary.why: Own the City has a different setting, storyline, teammates, and portable-specific design; the PSP/Zeebo lineage is best preserved with PPSSPP.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PSP version in PPSSPP at high internal resolution; use DS/GBA/Zeebo only for platform comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Separate companion to Carbon, not a direct version of the main campaign.

entries.title: Need for Speed: ProStreet

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route for the legal-track ProStreet pivot.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with compatibility fixes; use console/handheld versions only for comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster.

entries.title: Need for Speed: Undercover

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity and most configurable route for the cross-generation Undercover release.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with compatibility fixes; use console/handheld versions only for comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster.

entries.title: Need for Speed: Shift

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route for the Slightly Mad Studios simulation-leaning entry.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with PC compatibility fixes; use console/mobile versions only for comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster.

entries.title: Need for Speed: Nitro

primary.why: Nitro was built as a Nintendo-exclusive arcade-style entry, and Dolphin upscaling gives the Wii version the best fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Wii release in Dolphin at high internal resolution; use DS only for handheld comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster.

entries.title: Need for Speed: Nitro-X

primary.why: Nitro-X is the DSiWare update to Nitro with updated tracks, career revisions, and added rewards, so original DSi/3DS-family preservation is the route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on preserved DSi/3DS hardware or a compatible DSiWare preservation setup where legally available.

entries.remaster_caveats: Digital preservation entry; no remaster.

entries.title: Need for Speed: World

primary.why: World was the Windows-only MMO entry; official servers closed, so it is a preservation/shutdown row.
primary.how_to_play: No official live route remains; document the original client/server version and any legal preservation server separately.

entries.remaster_caveats: Official servers closed in 2015.

entries.title: Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit

primary.why: The remaster is the best modern route for Criterion's 2010 Hot Pursuit, with Windows providing the most configurable fidelity.
primary.how_to_play: Play Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit Remastered on Windows; use the original 2010 release only for historical comparison.

secondary.what_to_play: Sample the Wii version only if documenting alternate versions.
secondary.why: The Wii release was developed separately from Criterion's main game.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not confuse with Hot Pursuit 2 or the 1998 Hot Pursuit entry.

entries.title: Shift 2: Unleashed

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route for the Shift sequel.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with compatibility fixes; use PS3/Xbox 360 only for comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster.

entries.title: Need for Speed: The Run

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route for Black Box's final Need for Speed entry.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with compatibility fixes; use 3DS/Wii only for alternate portable/console comparisons.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster.

entries.title: Need for Speed: Most Wanted

primary.why: Criterion's 2012 reboot is best on Windows for fidelity and capture; it is a separate game from the 2005 Most Wanted.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with DLC where available; do not conflate this with the 2005 Black Box game.

secondary.exclusive_content: Wii U release includes platform-specific GamePad/social features and the Ultimate Speed Pack bundled as U content.
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the Wii U version only for platform-specific features.
secondary.why: The Wii U release has unique platform implementation.

entries.remaster_caveats: Distinct reboot from the 2005 Most Wanted.

entries.title: Need for Speed Rivals

primary.why: The Complete Edition includes the DLC packs, and Windows is the most configurable route for capture/fidelity.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows Complete Edition where available; note online-service status before archival capture.

entries.remaster_caveats: Check online-service state; base game remains playable offline where supported.

entries.title: Need for Speed: No Limits

emulation.notes: Use only with a documented app version.

primary.why: No Limits is a mobile-only original entry; Android gives the most controllable preservation/emulation path.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Android release or preserve a documented Android app version; iOS is equivalent for normal mobile play.

entries.remaster_caveats: Live-service mobile entry; record app version and content state.

entries.title: Need for Speed

primary.why: The 2015 reboot is best on Windows for fidelity and settings; the Deluxe Edition adds in-game starter/bonus content.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows Deluxe Edition where available; document online/service requirements before capture.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not confuse with the franchise name or the 1994 original.

entries.title: Need for Speed: Edge

primary.why: Edge was a regional free-to-play PC MMO based on Rivals and is now a shutdown preservation entry.
primary.how_to_play: No official live route remains; document the original regional client/server state if preserving.

entries.remaster_caveats: Preservation/shutdown entry.

entries.title: Need for Speed Payback

primary.why: Windows gives the best fidelity/settings route, and the Deluxe Edition bundles the most complete launch package.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows Deluxe Edition where available; document patch/DLC state.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster.

entries.title: Need for Speed Heat

primary.why: Windows offers the highest fidelity/settings route for Ghost Games' final Need for Speed title.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows Deluxe Edition where available; document patch and online state.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster.

entries.title: Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit Remastered

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route for Stellar Entertainment's remaster of Criterion's 2010 game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows remaster; it also serves as the primary route for the 2010 Hot Pursuit entry.

entries.remaster_caveats: Remaster of the 2010 Hot Pursuit reboot, not Hot Pursuit 2 or the 1998 game.

entries.title: Need for Speed Unbound

primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route, and EA's Ultimate Collection bundles the base game with post-launch content.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows Ultimate Collection/current patched build; document Volume content and online state.

entries.remaster_caveats: Live/post-launch content package; record current build and Volume content.

entries.title: Need for Speed Mobile

emulation.notes: Use only with documented region/app version.

primary.version: Need for Speed: Assemble regional mobile release
primary.why: The 2024 mobile entry is Android/iOS only and regionally released as Need for Speed: Assemble; Android is the more flexible preservation route.
primary.how_to_play: Play/preserve the Android regional release where legally available; document region, app version, and service state.

entries.remaster_caveats: Known as Need for Speed: Assemble in China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Macau.

entries.title: Need for Speed: Ferrari

primary.why: It was a planned Ferrari-focused project canceled before Porsche Unleashed shipped; no playable release/platform exists.
primary.how_to_play: Do not assign a play route unless a verified build/source appears.

entries.remaster_caveats: Canceled concept; keep as needs-research placeholder.
